calls.reason: CNN and WSJ-based reports show Khanmigo making math errors, and Inverse documents Pin hallucinations. But the hedged 'seem' comparison of the TED speakers is never actually assessed, so the claim as a whole can't be called.

This is a general principle. The 2025 RCT found students learned even from feedback that was always wrong, but they could spot the errors rather than being unsure what to believe, so the evidence doesn't directly test the claim.

The only evidence is a GenAI-Bench preprint on advanced compositions that ranks DALL-E 3 highly. It includes no test of alphabet or letter rendering, so the 'very buggy' claim is neither confirmed nor refuted.

The Verge's Humane review and Proof News's API tests of election questions show unreliability, but they cover one product and one narrow domain. That is too thin to settle a claim about every company's assistant.

OpenAI and Microsoft disrupted five state-linked groups by February 2024, and CrowdStrike's report, as covered by TIME, describes actors increasingly experimenting with LLMs. Use clearly grew from a near-zero start, even without a formal baseline.

OpenAI's own January 2024 post says it trains on public internet material as fair use with only an opt-out, and its licensing deals cover a few publishers. That points to most creators being unpaid and not consenting; the mission part is opinion.
